strengths: Addresses a critical and well-known bottleneck in equivariant GNNs, specifically the $O(|E|)$ memory and computation bottleneck caused by edge-centric tensor products and attention.

Proposes an elegant mathematical solution (Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification - EAAS) that rotates features to an SO(2) frame and leverages Wigner-6j recoupling to turn dense SO(3) contractions into sparse parity re-indexing operations, yielding a ~6x speedup.

Develops a highly practical, hardware-aware custom Triton kernel for node-centric streaming attention, avoiding the materialization of $O(|E|)$ intermediate tensors and enabling linear activation memory scaling.

Demonstrates excellent empirical results on SPICE and OMol25 datasets, scaling easily to 100,000 atoms on a single GPU where most existing equivariant architectures encounter Out-Of-Memory (OOM) failures.
Validates the practical utility of the model with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, showing physical stability and accurate radial distribution function (RDF) matching.
weaknesses: The mathematical formulation in the main body (especially Section 4.3 and the integration of Wigner-6j with SO(2) alignment) is dense and requires significant familiarity with spherical tensor algebra, which might limit accessibility for general readers.
The performance improvements are heavily tied to the custom Triton kernel implementation; there is limited discussion on portability to non-NVIDIA hardware architectures.
While the scaling performance is highly impressive, the impact of varying the maximum neighbor cutoff $K$ on the Triton kernel's performance could have been analyzed in more detail.

strengths: The proposed Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) elegantly simplifies dense SO(3) tensor contractions into sparse SO(2) blockwise operations, yielding a substantial practical speedup during convolutions.

The design of a custom fused Triton kernel for on-the-fly equivariant attention effectively overcomes the memory wall by eliminating the need to materialize O(|E|) edge tensors, shifting the bottleneck from memory-bound to compute-bound.

Excellent and thorough experimental evaluation demonstrating that E2Former-V2 maintains competitive or state-of-the-art predictive accuracy on SPICE and OMol25, while scaling reliably to 100,000 atoms without out-of-memory errors.

The manuscript is very well-written, clearly illustrating the mathematical derivations of EAAS in the appendix and highlighting the connection between group representation theory and hardware-aware deep learning.
weaknesses: The proposed method relies heavily on custom Triton kernels, which could limit immediate portability to platforms outside the NVIDIA/CUDA ecosystem.

While the paper details the forward pass of the fused attention kernel, the implementation details and complexity of the corresponding backward pass (especially regarding recomputation) are not thoroughly discussed in the main text.
A discussion on the impact of the online softmax's numerical stability when training with mixed precision (e.g., FP16 or BF16) would be highly valuable for practitioners.

strengths: Addresses a critical and well-known bottleneck in equivariant GNNs: the heavy O(|E|) memory and compute overhead of edge-centric tensor products.

Excellent hardware-aware co-design that eleganty unifies algebraic sparsification (SO(3) to SO(2) axis alignment and Wigner-6j recouping) with a custom fused Triton kernel (analogous to FlashAttention).
Strong mathematical foundation with solid proofs demonstrating how pole sparsity of solid spherical harmonics simplifies dense tensor products into sparse parity re-indexing.

Outstanding empirical results showing significant speedups (up to 20x in TFLOPS) and massive memory savings, allowing the model to scale to systems with 100,000 atoms where almost all prior models experience Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors.
Maintains or improves predictive accuracy on established molecular benchmarks (SPICE, OMol25) and shows strong physical fidelity in molecular dynamics simulations.
weaknesses: The details regarding the implementation of the backward pass for the custom Triton kernel are omitted. Since backward passes for fused streaming attention are notoriously complex to implement efficiently, more discussion on this would strengthen the paper.

The baseline comparisons for attention in Figure 1 ('FlashAttention' vs 'Traditional EGNN') could be more precisely defined to ensure readers fully understand what structural components are being compared.
A few minor typographical errors are present, such as 'code is avalible at' in the abstract and 'details of the tow datasets' in Section 5.1.

strengths: Addresses a major bottleneck in equivariant neural networks: the high memory footprint and latency associated with edge-centric tensor products (O(|E|) memory scaling).

Introduces Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS), which elegantly maps SO(3) tensor products to a local SO(2) aligned frame, collapsing dense tensor products into sparse parity-based re-indexing.

Proposes a hardware-aware, fused Triton kernel for on-the-fly equivariant attention, achieving up to 20x higher throughput and linear activation memory scaling with respect to the number of nodes (O(|V|)).

Extensive and rigorous evaluation across diverse datasets (SPICE, OMol25, and OC20 S2EF) showing that E2Former-V2 preserves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy while scaling reliably to 100k atoms without Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors.
Demonstrates the practical utility of the model through stable, long-time Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations of bulk water and a large protein system.
weaknesses: The reliance on custom Triton kernels limits the portability of the implementation to non-CUDA architectures.

To achieve a node-centric design, the model trades off explicit edge-level non-linearities (e.g., S^2 activations along the value path used in EquiformerV2/eSEN) for attention-modulated non-linearities. While the empirical results are strong, this design trade-off and its potential limitations on even more complex physical tasks could be discussed in greater depth in the main text.
The mathematical exposition in Section 4.3 (EAAS) is dense and could benefit from a more intuitive explanation of how the SO(3) to SO(2) change of basis yields the sparse structure.

strengths: The paper addresses a critical and well-known bottleneck in Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs): the $O(|E|)$ memory and computational footprint resulting from edge-centric tensor products and feature materialization.

The proposed Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) is mathematically elegant, leveraging pole sparsity in an aligned frame to reduce dense SO(3) tensor products into sparse, parity-based re-indexing operations.

The hardware-aware implementation of On-the-Fly Equivariant Attention via a fused Triton kernel is highly practical. It achieves a true $O(|V|)$ activation memory footprint, enabling scaling to 100k atoms without Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors.

Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks (SPICE, OMol25, OC20 S2EF) demonstrates that the proposed E2Former-V2 achieves state-of-the-art inference throughput while maintaining competitive predictive accuracy.

The real-world validation through molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on bulk water and a large solvated protein (~30k atoms) is excellent, proving the physical fidelity and numerical stability of the model's forces.
weaknesses: The custom Triton kernel currently operates primarily in FP32 (as acknowledged in Appendix J), which limits its ability to exploit low-precision Tensor Cores (e.g., FP16/BF16) that dense FlashAttention-style implementations utilize for massive speedups.

The EAAS approach requires computing rotation conjugation (alignment with $D_R$ and inverse-alignment with $D_{R^{-1}}$) for every operation. While the paper mentions a 1.5x speedup, a detailed breakdown of the computational overhead introduced by these coordinate transformations versus the savings from sparse re-indexing would benefit the main text.

Some of the key architectural differences and details regarding the reorganization of non-linearities (Appendix D) and baseline implementations (Appendix A) are deferred to the appendix, making the main text slightly self-contained but leaving important conceptual details out of the core narrative.

strengths: Significant performance and scalability gains: E2Former-V2 achieves linear activation memory scaling with the number of nodes O(|V|), allowing it to scale up to 100k atoms on a single GPU without out-of-memory (OOM) issues.

Excellent hardware-algorithm co-design: The combination of Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) and a custom fused Triton attention kernel provides a practical, hardware-friendly solution to the memory wall of equivariant transformers.

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation: The paper benchmarks the proposed model on multiple standard datasets (SPICE, OMol25, and OC20 S2EF), showing competitive or superior predictive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

Real-world physical validation: The authors successfully validate the physical stability of the model via long-term Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, reproducing bulk water radial distribution functions and stable protein trajectories.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty over E2Former-V1: The mathematical factorization that enables the O(|V|) scaling is conceptually inherited from E2Former-V1. The main contribution of this work lies in the engineering, custom kernel compilation, and the EAAS optimization.

Throughput gap with dense attention: Despite the substantial improvements over traditional EGNNs, the sparse Triton kernel still exhibits a performance gap in raw TFLOPS compared to dense FlashAttention (SDPA-Dense) due to the irregular nature of graph-structured neighbor gathers.

Highly complex mathematical derivations: The basis transformations (complex vs. real Clebsch-Gordan coefficients) in the appendix are highly intricate, which may present a steep learning curve for readers attempting to extend or modify the EAAS formulation.
